contexts.text: From this deep is heard a tumult as of a massacre.
The tumult of his chariots () = the derivative false doctrine.
When Divine truth descends towards lower things, it becomes at last tumultuous.

A tumult () = a contention for falsities against truths, and for evils against goods. ( = disturbance of all things of the Church. AE 601:4.) ( = dismay of all who are of the Church when visited and their evils disclosed. AE 659:22.)
Its waves are in an uproar () = reasonings about truths.
The dragonists are now in great agitation.
A tumult in the Lower Earth.
The tumult below ceased.
A tumult in the Heaven of Spirits from the conflict of opinions about Truths. Explained.
On a tumult under the sole of the left foot.
A tumultuous sound deep under the buttocks.
The antediluvians make a disturbance under their misty rock.
What the Lord said about the tumultuation of the sea, is to be under stood of heresies and controversies.
There then arose a tumult.
At this day there are such violent commotions around the man of the Church, mostly from the Hells.
Their tumult () = their threats, and cupidities of fighting, against truths. ( = dissension. AE 573:10.)
The tumult of strangers () = the irruption of falsities from evil.
To be tumultuous, etc. = the states (of goods and truths) when they perish, and falsities and evils enter in their place.
The last state of the old Church is described by a great tumultuation... (), by which is meant a change then, and the combat of the love of evil...
The tumult of the seas, and the tumult of the waves () = the disputations and reasonings of those who are beneath the Heavens, and are natural and sensuous.
A great tumult from the land of the north () = falsities fighting against truths, and evils against goods.
